scope.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

source.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

correspondence.explanation: All parameters and H001–H004 are retained: arbitrary characteristic-p field K, 0≤l<p, the complex sl₂ module and Chevalley triple, chosen highest-weight vector, and arbitrary admissible lattice. ComplexHyp uses trace-zero 2×2 complex matrices, the spanning Chevalley triple, representation law, dimension l.toNat+1, nontriviality, irreducibility and existence of a highest-weight vector; H001 identifies l.toNat with the nonnegative integer l. Admissible records coincident integer/complex bases and preservation by every divided power. U_Z-stability implies this generator preservation; conversely preservation extends to its generated unital integer algebra by closure under addition, integer scalars, composition and identity. Submodule ℤ V represents the additive subgroup. The tensor flip identifies VK=K⊗ℤM with the source M⊗ℤK, preserving the K action, and similarly identifies K⊗ℤLZ with the source Lie algebra. Target asserts nontriviality and produces Action, whose onM_spec, red_spec, red_lie, Lift and gen_spec specify exactly the induced lattice Lie action and its three generators. These formulas uniquely determine the operators on pure tensors and hence everywhere. Thus Target yields the source assertion for the canonical action; conversely that assertion together with the constructed action gives Target. Nontriviality is equivalent to a nonzero vector, and bottom/top submodules mean zero/the whole space. Stability under the generators is equivalent to stability under their scalar-extended integer span, by linearity and closure of subspaces under linear combinations. T007/T010 construct Action; T020/T021 check the tensor conversions actually used, and T029 proves Target using the same action and transported basis from T025. No algebraic closure or separation of reduced weights is assumed, including l=0 and p=2.
